rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly, so the table pushes obfuscation strength up while respecting this profile's nature as a floating-point compute benchmark (fbench, whetstone, flops, himenobmtxpa): hot FP loops make control-flow flattening and bogus-control-flow the most expensive accelerators, so FLA and BCF get mid-range security weights with elevated RuntimeCost penalties so they apply selectively rather than blanket. SUB is nearly free and highly disruptive to pattern matching, so it carries the highest security/diversity weights with low cost penalties; SPLIT and IGV are similarly cheap and compound with SUB by fragmenting and re-typing the dataflow, improving diversity at minimal overhead. ICALL and IBR add strong anti-analysis value (opaque indirect calls and branches defeat static CFG recovery) and, with round 1 confirming correctness headroom on this tiny 2-function binary, their weights are raised with moderate runtime penalties since call/branch overhead is amortized outside the innermost FP loops. CorrectnessRisk stays low across the board to preserve the verified pass status, with the highest caution reserved for FLA and IBR, which interact most with loop structure and branch semantics.
